name: Context Pruning
question: Does the model need everything in the context window?
summary: Long-running agents pile up history, tool output and retrieved documents, and every token is paid for again on every turn. Pruning keeps the context small: summarize old turns, drop tool results once they have been used, retrieve fewer and better chunks, and compress prompts.
useCases: Long conversations and multi-hour agent sessions
Agents that read large files, logs or web pages
RAG pipelines that stuff many chunks into every prompt

items.detail: keep the last N turns word for word
older turns become a running summary
drop raw outputs once they have been used
fewer, re-ranked chunks instead of the top 20
store facts outside the context and retrieve on demand

steps: Plot context size per turn for your longest sessions
Summarize when context crosses a threshold, keeping decisions and open tasks
Clear bulky tool outputs after extracting what matters
Re-run long-task evals to confirm nothing important was lost
pitfalls: Summaries drop details the agent needs later
Aggressive pruning breaks references to earlier turns
Pruning changes the prompt prefix, which can cancel prompt-cache savings
remember: Every token is paid for on every turn.
caption: Totals are the sum of context size over 21 turns in this example. Summarizing at 16k keeps each turn cheap.

comparison.best: Can drop details the agent needs

code.text: return sum(len(enc.encode(m["content"])) for m in msgs)
m["content"] = "[tool output cleared; key values recorded]"
note = llm("Summarize decisions, client facts, figures and open tasks:\n"
# Eval: replay 30 day-long sessions; check answers that need early facts

steps.title: Plot context per turn
steps.text: Every turn resends the whole history. Context here grows by about 1.9k tokens a turn and reaches 40k by turn 20.

steps.title: Set a threshold
steps.text: Decide when to act: once context passes 16k tokens, prune before the next call.

steps.title: Keep recent turns word for word
steps.text: The last 4 turns stay verbatim, because the next reply usually depends on them.

steps.title: Summarize the older turns
steps.text: Everything older becomes a short note that keeps decisions, client facts, figures and open tasks. Context drops back and grows again.

steps.title: Clear used tool output
steps.text: Raw statement extracts are replaced by a placeholder once their key figures have been recorded in a reply.

steps.title: Check nothing was lost
steps.text: Replay long sessions and test questions that need early facts. Input paid over turns 0–20 falls from 441k to 190k tokens.

pros: Stops cost from compounding with every turn
Keeps long sessions under the context limit
Smaller contexts are faster and often more focused
Tool-result clearing is almost free to implement
cons: Summaries can drop details the agent needs later
Rewriting history breaks prompt-cache reuse after the change point
Needs long-session evals to prove nothing was lost
avoidWhen: Sessions are short and never approach the threshold
Every earlier detail must be kept word for word (store it externally and retrieve it)

playgroundGuide.scenario: A relationship-manager copilot stays open all day with one client. Each turn adds conversation and a statement extract. At turn 20 the client asks a question that needs two early facts: their preference for debt funds (turn 2) and their FD balance of INR 4.2 lakh (turn 5). You choose how to keep the context small without losing them.

practice.scenario: A relationship-manager copilot stays open all day with one client. Once the context passes 16k tokens, older turns are summarized into a short note such as “prefers debt funds; SIP review on the 15th”. Raw statement extracts are dropped once their figures have been recorded.

industries.use: Long-running advisor copilots keep a running client summary
Multi-day tickets carry a summary, not the full thread
Coding agents clear old test logs after reading them

practice.analogy: Meeting minutes. Nobody replays the whole recording; the next meeting starts from the one-page summary.

library.name: tiktoken + your LLM
library.what: Count tokens precisely, then summarize with any model. For compression without summaries, LLMLingua is the common choice.

numericDrill.question: Context starts at 2k tokens and grows by 2k per turn, so turns 1–5 send 2k, 4k, 6k, 8k and 10k. If pruning caps every turn at 6k, what is the new total input, in thousands?
numericDrill.answer: Before: 30k. After: 2 + 4 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 24k. The saving grows with every extra turn.

interview.question: How do you prune without losing important information?
interview.answer: Keep recent turns word for word, summarize older ones into decisions, facts and open tasks, clear tool outputs once their key values are recorded, and keep durable facts in external memory the agent can query. Validate on long-task evals.

interview.question: How does pruning interact with prompt caching?
interview.answer: Caching rewards a stable prefix, and pruning rewrites history, invalidating the cache after the change point. Prune in larger, less frequent steps and keep the system prompt and tools above the pruned region.

mistakes.mistake: Cutting from the start and losing the system prompt
mistakes.fix: Keep system prompt and tools; prune the middle
Keep decisions, facts and pending actions in every summary

quiz.question: Context starts at 3k tokens and grows by 3k a turn, so turns 1–6 send 3k, 6k, 9k, 12k, 15k and 18k. If pruning caps every turn at 9k, what is the total input?
Why does each turn of a long advisor chat cost more than the one before?
options: The whole history is resent and paid for on every turn
quiz.explanation: Models keep no state between calls, so every turn resends the growing context.

quiz.question: What should a running summary of a multi-day support ticket keep? Select all that apply.
options: Key figures such as amounts and dates
quiz.explanation: A summary must keep what later turns depend on. Pleasantries only cost tokens.

quiz.question: A sliding window keeps the last 6 turns. The plan the customer chose at turn 2 is forgotten by turn 12. What is the fix?
options: Summarize older turns, keeping key facts, instead of dropping them
quiz.explanation: Windows drop everything outside them. A summary keeps the facts while still shrinking the context.

quiz.question: A coding agent reads an 8,000-token test log once to find two failing tests. What should happen to the log?
options: Clear the raw log once the failing tests are recorded
Move it to the top of the prompt
quiz.explanation: Tool output that has been used only costs tokens on every later step. Record what matters, then clear it.

quiz.question: Each of 10 turns adds a 2,000-token tool output that is only needed on the turn it arrives. How many input tokens does clearing earlier outputs save across the session?
quiz.explanation: Without clearing, turn t carries (t − 1) old outputs: 2,000 × (0 + 1 + … + 9) = 2,000 × 45 = 90,000 tokens.

quiz.question: A contract Q&A pipeline puts the top 20 retrieved chunks in every prompt. Which changes cut retrieved context sensibly? Select all that apply.
options: Retrieve fewer chunks and re-rank them
Compress chunks with a tool such as LLMLingua
quiz.explanation: Fewer, better and de-duplicated chunks, or compressed ones, shrink input. Retrieving more does the opposite.

quiz.question: Pruning on every turn broke prompt caching for a tutor bot. Which design keeps both?
options: Put the summary before the system prompt
Keep the system prompt and tools above the pruned region and prune less often
Prune on every turn but smaller amounts
quiz.explanation: A stable top section keeps cache hits; infrequent pruning lets the rewritten history be reused for many turns.

quiz.question: A clinical assistant’s summary dropped a patient’s allergy. What is the best safeguard?
options: Pin critical facts outside the summarized region and test long sessions
quiz.explanation: Facts that must never be lost belong in a pinned section or external store, with evals that check them.

quiz.question: An agent must remember each policyholder’s preferences across sessions months apart. Which tool fits?
quiz.explanation: Mem0 stores memories outside the context and retrieves them when relevant.

quiz.question: You want to shrink long retrieved passages by removing low-information tokens before they reach the model. Which tool fits?
quiz.explanation: LLMLingua compresses prompts by dropping tokens that carry little information.

quiz.question: A summary call reads 14k tokens once and replaces them with a 1k summary. Each of the next 10 turns then sends 13k fewer tokens. Ignoring output, what is the net input saving?
quiz.explanation: 10 × 13k = 130k saved, minus the 14k the summary call read: 116k.

quiz.question: Which symptoms show that context pruning is needed? Select all that apply.
options: Cost per turn rises steadily in long sessions
Sessions hit the context window limit
Old tool outputs and retrieved chunks dominate input tokens
quiz.explanation: Growing per-turn cost and bloated contexts are the signal. Two-turn sessions have little to prune.

quiz.question: Besides cost, why can a smaller context improve answers?
options: Models can miss information buried in the middle of long contexts
quiz.explanation: Studies such as “Lost in the middle” found models use information at the start and end of long contexts better than the middle.

quiz.question: Which parts of a shopping assistant’s context should normally survive pruning? Select all that apply.
options: Raw tool outputs that have already been used
quiz.explanation: Keep the instructions, the recent turns and pinned facts. Used tool output is the first thing to clear.

quiz.question: Context is 4k at turn 1 and grows by 2k a turn. You summarize when context is more than 12k. On which turn does the first summary happen?
quiz.explanation: Context at turn t is 2t + 2 thousand: turn 5 is exactly 12k, turn 6 is 14k, the first above the threshold.

quiz.question: A dispatch assistant needs shipment details from conversations up to three weeks old. What is the best approach?
options: Keep all three weeks in the context
Store facts externally and retrieve them by shipment ID
quiz.explanation: External memory keeps durable facts without carrying them in every prompt.

quiz.question: What are the costs or risks of summarization-based pruning? Select all that apply.
quiz.explanation: Summaries cost a call, can lose information and change the prefix. They do not change the window size.

quiz.question: In a quote-lookup assistant, only the last three turns ever matter. What is enough?
options: A sliding window over the recent turns
A knowledge graph of the whole conversation
quiz.explanation: When older turns are never needed, a simple window is the cheapest correct choice.

quiz.question: After pruning, a copilot sends a 2k system prompt, a 1k summary and the last 4 turns of 1.5k each. What is the context size?
quiz.explanation: 2k + 1k + 4 × 1.5k = 9k tokens.
